lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.unitTitle: Circles, Angles, Area, and Surface Area
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: surface area and volume

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: A rectangular prism has length 5, width 11, and height 9 (all in units). What is its exact surface area, in square units?
What is the exact volume of a rectangular prism with length 5, width 4, and height 9 1/2 (units)? Give your answer in cubic units.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: A circle has a diameter of 13 cm. What is its exact circumference? Express your answer as a multiple of π.
A circle has a circumference of 8π cm. What is its exact diameter?
A circle has a radius of 10 ft. What is its exact area? Express your answer as a multiple of π (use a fraction for the coefficient if it is not a whole number).
A circle's radius equals its circumference divided by 2π. A circle has a circumference of 7π in. Use this relationship to find the circle's exact area, as a multiple of π.
Two angles are supplementary. One angle measures 24°. What is the measure of the other angle?
Two lines intersect, forming vertical angles that measure (4x + 10)° and (2x + 30)°. Vertical angles are congruent. Find the value of x and the measure of the angles.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: Two angles are supplementary. Their measures are (6x + 7)° and (4x + 103)°. Find the value of x and the measure of each angle.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: Three angles lie along a straight line and measure 3°, 5°, 80°, and x°. What is the value of x?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
